title: Resilience rollforward roadmap & gatebook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working product-ops artifact that ties the Q2 product roadmap lanes (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) to a resilience-first launch framework. The goal: ensure each feature has measurable gates (KPI thresholds + test signals), an explicit rollforward window, and runbooks for graceful degradation. Note: this is intentionally operational (checklists + quick tables) — not the canonical spec; link to Confluence above for formal runbooks.

Quick summary (one-line):
- Treat first production ramp as an experiment: go-live when acceptance metrics + stability signals meet predefined thresholds; otherwise, hold and iterate.

Owners & contacts:
- Launch owner: Leah Martinez (product-ops) — primary coordinator, greenlight facilitator
- SRE liaison: Devon Patel — infra & capacity gating
- Observability: Sana Iqbal — dashboards, alert tuning, post-launch triage lead
- Release engineer: Marco Ruiz — CI/CD, canary pipelines, rollback automation
- Support escalation: Priya Nambiar (customer-success)

Roadmap lanes covered:
- Hosted API: V2 rate-limiter changes + streaming opt-in
- Dedicated: reserved capacity autoscale policy experiment for baseline latency
- Private: VPC onboarding automation + KMS rotation flow

Rollforward philosophy (short):
1) Canary-first: small internal traffic -> beta customers -> open rollout.
2) Gate on metrics at each stage (functional, quality, cost, infra).
3) If any gate trips, trigger either immediate rollback or controlled throttle depending on severity.
4) Rollforward allowed only after remediation paired with regression test run and sign-off from SRE + product owner.

KPI tracker (text-table for copying into a sheet) — each row = feature lane / gate stage:
Columns: lane | stage | lead | functional-pass | p95-latency-ms | error-rate-5m | cost-est-change | adoption-signal | gate-action
Hosted-V2 | internal-canary | Leah M | yes | < 120ms | < 0.5% | +3% | internal-usage >= 100 reqs | progress to beta
Hosted-V2 | beta-customers | Leah M | yes | < 150ms | < 1.0% | +5% | NPS >= 30 | progress to open rollout
Dedicated-autoscale | canary | Marco R | yes | < 100ms | < 0.3% | -8% | sustained-20m at target throughput | scale to regional pool
Private-vpc-onboard | enterprise-pilot | Sana I | yes | < 180ms | < 0.2% | +2% | pilot-customer-successful | proceed with KMS schedule

Gate thresholds (decision heuristics):
- Functional-pass: automated smoke tests 100% pass for 30m continuous traffic
- Latency: p95 must be within 20% of baseline for that lane or we hold
- Error rate: rolling 5m > 1% => immediate canary pause; > 2% => rollback
- Cost: delta > +15% token unit cost triggers cost-review (do not block rollout unless combined with other signals)
- Adoption: meaningful usage (see table per lane) required to validate real-world performance

Traffic shaping and throttles (ops knobs):
- Canary weight schedule: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%; each step min 1 hour and must satisfy gates
- Auto-throttle rule: if p95 > gate threshold OR error-rate > 1% for 10m, cut traffic by 50% and notify on-call.
- Fallback model routing: route 10% to older stable model variant if classification/regression observed

Pre-launch checklist (must be green before canary):
- [ ] Release artifact built and signed (Marco)
- [ ] Canary pipeline configured and smoke tests in CI (Marco)
- [ ] Capacity validation: required GPUs/nodes available in region (Devon)
- [ ] Observability: dashboards + alert thresholds created and tested (Sana)
- [ ] Chaos-lite test: simulate node loss & verify graceful degradation (SRE)
- [ ] Security: KMS keys staged, access policies reviewed (Security)
- [ ] Data privacy: data flow diagram updated for telemetry (Product-privacy)
- [ ] Communications: internal Slack channel created + customer pilot comms draft (Leah)

Launch day runbook (canary -> beta -> open):
- T-0 start canary at 1% internal traffic. Monitor 30m window.
- If all gates pass, promote to 5% and run another 1h window.
- Beta invitation: send to 5 pilot customers when canary 20% stable for 2h. Capture qualitative feedback.
- Escalation: any critical regression -> call SRE on-call, page with tag "launch-critical", open postmortem at incident severity >= Sev2.

Contingency playbook (short scenarios):
- Scenario A: sudden p95 spike (no error-rate change): enable auto-throttle, capture flamegraphs, revert kernel selection via infra toggle. If still degraded after 15m, rollback canary.
- Scenario B: increased error rate > 2%: immediate roll-back to previous stable release; preserve logs for triage; initiate hotfix branch.
- Scenario C: cost unexpectedly +25%: pause further rollout, revert batching/quantization changes, open cost-review war room.

Post-launch acceptance window (48h):
- Required: no Sev2 incidents attributable to the release, adoption metrics meeting runway expectations, and customer feedback triaged.
- Sign-off route: SRE (Devon) + Observability (Sana) + Product-ops (Leah) -> mark 'release accepted' in tracker.

Quick notes / unresolved items (working):
- Need a standard definition for "meaningful adoption" per lane (suggestion: 1% of weekly active users for hosted; sustained 10k QPS-sample for Dedicated).
- Decide whether cost gates should be soft for early experimentations (proposal: soft for first 2 weeks).
- Slack thread: #launch-v2-discuss (see linked_artifacts above).

Next steps (for this doc):
- Lock down the numerical adoption thresholds (action: Leah + growth, due 2026-03-17).
- Create short daily post-launch checklist (Sana to author).
- Convert KPI table into a living sheet and wire alerts to thresholds (Marco + Devon).

Appendix: quick copy-paste metrics for dashboards:
- Hosted-V2: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5m error rate, token-cost-per-1k, requests-per-minute
- Dedicated: tail-latency distribution, scheduled-scale events, queue depth, model-kv-cache hit-rate
- Private: onboarding success rate, KMS rotation latency, network egress errors

Tags and quick links: this doc is a working gatebook for Q2 launches; store final runbooks in Confluence-1203 and mark the tracker with JIRA-PLT-8821 once final.

-- end of working draft --

Notes to self: keep this doc terse; move policy language into Confluence and keep this as the checklist + quick decision heuristics artifact.
